scope.title: Persisted attachment constrained to a recoverable minimal checkpoint

decision.reason: A bounded attachment binding (five reference kinds) validates sha256 hash, owner and TTL; recovery is a pure function that flags missing/invalid/expired/conflicting bindings into explicit states, de-duplicates identical refs and never re-runs a side effect.

attachmentBinding.recovery: pure: no input mutation, identical digest on repeat, no side-effect replay, deterministic order
attachmentBinding.repair: missing/invalid/expired excluded from recovered; same-ref different-hash -> conflict (first kept); identical ref deduped

residual.assembly: The binding validator/recovery is provided; wiring it into a concrete persisted-attachment write path is integration-layer work.
residual.scope: No new store, no daemon, no auto-writeback; no default/lock/approval change.

independentVerification.detail: Tests assert deterministic recovery/dedup, per-input state classification (missing/invalid hash, missing owner, expired, conflict) and purity (input unchanged, identical digest on repeat). No separate second-agent verifier role was run.

acceptanceCriteria.note: Only five reference kinds are allowed; no arbitrary cursor or blob.
Missing/invalid sha256 hash, missing owner and expired TTL each map to an explicit state and are excluded from recovery.
Same attachmentRef with a different hash becomes an explicit conflict state (first binding kept); identical refs are de-duplicated.
Recovery does not mutate input, returns an identical digest on repeat, and re-runs no side effect.
Recovered bindings are sorted by attachmentRef and the result carries a digest.
4 tests pass, tsgo:core 0, scoped lint 0, harness validate/dry-run pass, comms 0, credential scan 0 hits, SHA256SUMS verifiable.

notMeasured: Integration into a concrete persisted-attachment write path.
A separate second-agent independent verifier role.
